evidence.description:
The
block renders the text "HELLO WORLD" directly below the

Task list

heading in src/App.tsx.

The block is a semantic <section> with a non-empty aria-label, exposing the implicit ARIA role "region" with accessible name "Welcome"; verified by the new unit test's getByRole("region", { name: "Welcome" }) query succeeding.
New unit test "shows the welcome block with the exact text HELLO WORLD" in src/App.test.tsx asserts toHaveTextContent("HELLO WORLD"); ran via npm run test:unit, saw it pass (11/11 tests passed).

Existing e2e test in e2e/app.spec.ts updated with an assertion that page.getByRole("region", { name: "Welcome" }) has text "HELLO WORLD" right after page load. Not executed locally per sandbox restriction on launching browsers on macOS; left for the coordinator's checks.

All pre-existing unit tests (filtering, starring, task count) continue to pass unmodified (11/11 total including the new test); lint, typecheck and build all pass locally with no changes to domain/storage logic. e2e run left to coordinator.

reason: Added a static `<section aria-label="Welcome">HELLO WORLD</section>` block in src/App.tsx between the "Task list" heading and the status filter, exactly as specified in the approved plan. Added a unit test asserting the region renders with the exact text "HELLO WORLD", and updated the existing e2e test to assert the block is visible on load. Lint, typecheck, unit tests (11/11 passing) and build all pass locally; e2e execution is left to the coordinator per sandbox restrictions on launching browsers on macOS.
